items.evidence: Repository facts and factual editorial fields map to F1-F9, which cite GitHub metadata, the official README, Skill, manifest, and release.
I1-I2 and D1-D3 clearly label the reuse reasoning and separate all three proposed products from built-in Archify behavior.
GitHub ID, canonical name, MIT license, active state, raw counts, push time, and fetchedAt match the 2026-08-30 metadata snapshot.
The note records snapshot staleness, the main-versus-stable release boundary, direction status, and the absence of demand research.
The hook uses Archify's distinctive transformation from a complex system into an explorable map without generic praise or a feature list.
The summary states the codebase or description input, typed JSON and validation process, five viewing modes, interaction, and export outcomes.
Five diagram types, typed source, validation gates, interactive exploration, and exports are all supported by F2-F5.
AI agent, JSON, HTML/SVG, Node.js, and JSON Schema are retained only where they explain generation, portability, runtime, or validation.
The hook establishes one memorable transformation; the summary independently explains the complete existing-product workflow.
The summary describes Archify only, while meaning explains why its verified generation and delivery pipeline can support focused products.
Each opportunity connects a verified capability or technical-authoring friction to guided learning, privacy review, or incident storytelling.
The original technical audience is distinct from three narrower audiences; every approach is a journey and every scope is a 5-item minimum set.
Each direction names a concrete user and recurring situation: explaining a Vibe project, checking household data, or reviewing an incident.
Each direction states its input, transformation steps, reused diagram mode, and visible interactive page, checklist, or replayable path.
D1-D3 cite F2-F5 and change both the authoring workflow and result instead of merely adding AI, mobile access, translation, or a new label.
All scopes contain five necessary functions that close the promised input-to-outcome journey without schedules or optional roadmap items.
The directions differ across audience, repository versus household versus incident input, core workflow, and visible outcome.
The directions create concrete understanding, privacy visibility, and shared incident comprehension rather than promising generic efficiency or growth.
The Vibe learning direction and household privacy direction primarily serve learning, personal understanding, and family value.
